**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

**What I found**

- The term provisions are located in the mis-numbered tail of § 12: **¶p0078 (13. TERM)** — one-year initial term auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal.
- **¶p0079 (14. TERMINATION)** contains the only Client exit: "Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide … until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides … notice of its election to terminate."

**Why it deviates**

1. It is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic, not an express convenience right, and the effective date can run up to ~60 days.
2. It is qualified by a "Section 4" that does not exist in the document (the outline skips 3, 4, 6, 9, 11), leaving the right subject to unknown conditions — and § 5(a)/§ 6 reference **minimum monthly fees** that could be asserted post-termination.
3. No refund of prepaid fees and no express bar on early-termination charges.

**Direction check:** Vendor has no mid-term convenience right — only 30-day non-renewal at the end of each annual term — so no vendor-side deletion was required. Because the committed term is 12 months (not multi-year), this is a drafting-quality deviation rather than a missing-behaviour finding.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, ¶p0079):** Client may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice; TrueLink services continue to the effective date; refund of prepaid fees; no early-termination fee, penalty or minimum-fee obligation for periods after termination. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
